- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; adjust downward bias by 5–10% relative to recent low.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment flips from bullish to bearish (or vice versa), model lags; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift within 2–3 days.
- If model shows steady upward trend but true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline), reduce forecast slope by 10–20%.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >15% from model, check sentiment history: if sentiment is neutral or mixed, model may be overfitting; use rolling 7-day average as anchor.
